<div class="cg-ill__frame" markdown="1">
<div class="cg-ill__eyebrow">Part Route</div>
<h3 class="cg-ill__title">How The Spatial Analysis Toolkit Fits Together</h3>
<p class="cg-ill__lede">This part is easier to learn when the chapters read like a toolkit instead of an arbitrary list. The route starts with predicates and rasters, moves through vector operations, then builds up to terrain and monitoring workflows.</p>
<div class="cg-ill__route-map">
<div class="cg-ill__route-stage">
<span class="cg-ill__route-kicker">Start Here</span>
<h4>Predicates and Raster Basics</h4>
<p>Learn how spatial relationships and cell grids represent geographic space.</p>
<ul>
<li>Point-in-polygon</li>
<li>Raster resampling</li>
<li>Map algebra</li>
<li>Raster classification</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="cg-ill__route-arrow">→</div>
<div class="cg-ill__route-stage">
<span class="cg-ill__route-kicker">Then Build</span>
<h4>Vector Analysis Toolkit</h4>
<p>Turn geometry into queries about distance, overlap, and matching features.</p>
<ul>
<li>Buffers</li>
<li>Overlay</li>
<li>Spatial joins</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="cg-ill__route-arrow">→</div>
<div class="cg-ill__route-stage">
<span class="cg-ill__route-kicker">Apply To Terrain</span>
<h4>Surface and Network Reasoning</h4>
<p>Use elevation and friction surfaces to reason about visibility, flow, and movement.</p>
<ul>
<li>Viewsheds</li>
<li>Least-cost paths</li>
<li>Watersheds</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="cg-ill__route-footer">
<div class="cg-ill__route-note">
<strong>Extend the toolkit:</strong> classification, change detection, and time-series chapters show how these same spatial primitives support remote sensing workflows.
</div>
</div>
</div>
<figcaption>The part works best as a progression: represent space, operate on geometry and rasters, then combine those operations into terrain and monitoring models.</figcaption>
</figure>
